title: Norfolk Southern employees give back on 9/11 National Day of Service
body_markdown:
On the 25th anniversary of 9/11, Norfolk Southern employees came together in Atlanta to honor a National Day of Service and Remembrance by helping provide meals for neighbors facing food insecurity.


The Atlanta event, hosted by[911 Day](https://www.911day.org/) and sponsored by Norfolk Southern, brought together 50 NS employees and volunteers from across the community to pack 356,400 meals for neighbors facing food insecurity.


**Why it matters:** September 11 is a day to remember those who were lost and honor the first responders, recovery workers, service members, and volunteers who stepped forward in the aftermath. Twenty-five years later, acts of service continue that legacy by bringing people together to support their communities.


**A nationwide day of service**


The Atlanta meal pack was part of a nationwide effort expected to bring together 50,000 volunteers to pack more than 18 million meals across more than 50 U.S. cities.


For Norfolk Southern employees, the afternoon offered a meaningful way to mark the anniversary alongside colleagues and community members.


**The bigger picture**


Service is one way Norfolk Southern employees make a difference in the communities where they live and work. By joining the 9/11 Day Meal Pack, Team NS is helping carry forward a tradition that transforms remembrance into action and honors the spirit of service that emerged in the days following September 11.


**Learn more about Norfolk Southern’s**[community impact](https://www.norfolksouthern.com/en/commitments/in-your-community/community-impact) **.**
